boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Bear River record (January 29, 1863) in Expedition from Camp Douglas, Utah, to Cache Valley, Idaho [January 1863]. The march from Camp Douglas from January 22 is context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the District of Utah and Shoshoni Indians without figures; the live field reads 0. The frozen description gives about 300 Shoshoni warriors. Connor moved with 220 cavalry and an infantry company with two howitzers, and says no more than 200 were engaged because of frozen feet and detachments, against about 300 warriors; Wright repeats 200 engaged. Bancroft gives some three hundred Shoshones and Bannacks and about two hundred of Connor's men, of a command of 300 volunteers.
claims.rationale: Column, engaged and opponent-estimated figures: 220 cavalry left Camp Douglas on January 24; 200 engaged and about 300 warriors refer to January 29 by Connor's estimate; Bancroft's 300 volunteers is the whole command and follows Connor. No account by the Shoshone side was inspected; their numbers, aims and losses come from their opponents, NPS or Bancroft's summaries. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.rationale: A natural ravine improved by its defenders; tag unresolved. No map verification.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Colonel Patrick Edward Connor and Bear Hunter (no rank recorded); the live page tags Bear Hunter [CS], not adopted. Connor says McGarry had dismounted the cavalry and engaged before he arrived, and that he then ordered McGarry to turn the left flank and the infantry across the river; NPS says an early frontal attack was repulsed before Connor took over. Connor lists Bear Hunter among the dead.
claims.rationale: Command roles from an interested report and the NPS summary; no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory (massacre) and the frozen other name Massacre at Boa Ogoi; the live result reads Union Victory. Wright calls the victory complete and Connor says the fight lasted from about 6 to 10 o'clock. NPS says the troops killed most of the warriors and a number of women, children and old men. Bancroft reports the band almost annihilated and remarks that, had the Indians committed the deed, it would be called a butchery or a massacre.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The characterizations (victory, battle, massacre) are the sources' and are not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 451 (US 67; I 384); the live field reads 315 (US 65; CS 250). Connor found 224 bodies and did not examine the field, and left a number of captive women and children read 'ICO' in OCR (not decoded). Wright gives 14 killed and 4 officers and 49 men wounded, of whom 1 officer and 5 men died. Bancroft gives fourteen killed and forty-nine wounded and summarizes two local accounts: 200 killed, and 368 dead counted by an eyewitness from Franklin, about 90 of them women and children.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Wright's 14 + 4 + 49 equals the frozen US 67; the frozen 384 and live 250 are not traced.

open_questions: Connor's unprinted list of killed and wounded, the Shoshone account, Tullidge's History of Salt Lake City and the local accounts Bancroft cites (Logan branch record, Martineau), Mormon settlers' records and maps remain deferred. Bancroft dates the troops' approach to 'the 28th', against Connor's and the frozen January 29; not resolved.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Connor's February 6, 1863 report is an interested account; Wright's transmittal depends on it. Hubert Howe Bancroft's History of Utah (1889) is a retrospective history that uses Connor's despatch as printed by Tullidge and two local accounts; it is not independent of Connor for the figures it takes from him. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.

No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Participants are named as the sources name them; characterizations in the sources (including 'hostile', 'savages', 'massacre' or 'battle') are quoted as the sources' own words and not adopted.
